blocks.h2: When to Replace Your Water Heater

tiles.body: Once water comes from the tank body, the inside is rusting through. It can't be patched.
Check the date on the label. A heater that old is living on borrowed time, even if it still works.
A second or third repair in a couple of years usually costs more than a new heater over time.
A finished basement bathroom or more people at home can outgrow a 40-gallon tank.

blocks.h2: How We Install Your New Water Heater
blocks.intro: A clean swap, done to code:

steps.body: We ask how many people, bathrooms and big tubs you have, then match the capacity and recovery rate.
New shutoff valve, flexible connectors, an expansion tank where needed and a check of the gas line and vent.
We drain and haul the old heater away, test the new one and show you the controls.

blocks.h2: Water Heater Installs in Arlington Heights Homes
blocks.intro: Most homes here were built between 1940 and 1989, and the basement setup around the heater often needs updating when it's replaced.

items.body: If your furnace was replaced with a high-efficiency model that vents out the side wall, your new water heater may not draft well alone in the old chimney. We check it and may recommend a chimney liner or a power-vent heater.
Some older basements have the heater squeezed in a small space next to the furnace. We measure before we quote so the new unit fits with proper clearances.
If you added a bathroom or have teenagers, a larger tank, a high-recovery model or a [tankless water heater](/arlington-heights/tankless-water-heater) may serve you better.

blocks.h2: Water Heater Installation Questions From Arlington Heights Homeowners

items.q: What size water heater do I need?
items.preview: Most families do well with 40 to 50 gallons. We size it to your home.
items.answer: Most households of three or four do well with a 40 or 50 gallon tank. Larger households, big soaking tubs or a basement bathroom may need more capacity or faster recovery. We'll ask a few questions and size it right.

items.q: Can you replace my water heater the same day?
items.preview: Often, yes, when the unit is in stock.
items.answer: Often, yes. Standard tank heaters are usually available, so a leaking heater can often be replaced in one visit. Specialty or tankless units may take longer to get.

items.q: Do I need an expansion tank?
items.preview: If your home has a check valve or pressure reducer, usually yes.
items.answer: If your water service has a check valve or pressure reducing valve, the water has nowhere to go when it heats and expands. An expansion tank absorbs that pressure and protects the heater and your fixtures. We'll check during the visit.

items.preview: It depends on your hot water use, gas line and venting.
items.answer: It can make sense if you want endless hot water and lower standby losses. It may need a larger gas line and new venting. See [tankless water heaters](/arlington-heights/tankless-water-heater) for the details.

items.q: How much does water heater installation cost in Arlington Heights?
items.preview: It depends on the type, size and any code updates. You get a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the type and size of heater, the venting and any code updates needed. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins.
